rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods, Experiment design - two-year field experiment (2015-2016) at Sichuan Agricultural University farm comparing three row configurations (A1, A2, CK) with measurements of PAR, biomass, chlorophyll, photosynthesis, leaf anatomy and yield.
rows.notes: The study is a field experiment on shading and light recovery of soybean in a maize-soybean relay-strip intercropping system. It contains no irrigation treatment, no drip fertigation, no root development measurements and no corn yield data. The results concern soybean canopy light environment, morphology, leaf anatomy, photosynthetic rate and soybean yield per plant under different row configurations versus sole cropping. Nothing in the study supports a 34% increase in corn root development or higher grain yield from drip fertigation; the claim appears misattributed.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study does not address irrigation technology at all; the citation seems to be a misattribution.
